sq.QUESTION_DESC: A tightly stretched string of length 21 is fastened at both ends. The midpoint of the string is displaced to a distance b and released from rest in this position. Write the initial conditions.

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
\(\text{Wave equation: \(y_{tt} = c^2 y_{xx}.\) BCs: \(y(0,t)=0\), \(y(l,t)=0.\) Initial conditions: \(y(x,0)= kx(l-x)\), \(y_t(x,0)=0.\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{General solution: \(y(x,t)= \sum \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right)\left[C_n \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right)+D_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right)\right].\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(y_t(x,0)=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(D_n=0.\) So \(y(x,t)= \sum C_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right).\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(y(x,0)= \sum C_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) = kx(l-x).\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{Expand \(f(x)=kx(l-x)\) in Fourier sine series on \((0,l)\): \(f(x)= \sum b_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right)\) with \(b_n = \dfrac{2}{l} \int_0^l kx(l-x) \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) dx.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Compute \(b_n\): integration gives \(b_n = \dfrac{8kl^2}{n^3\pi^3}\) for \(n\) odd, \(0\) for \(n\) even.}\) (3 Marks)
\(\text{Thus \(C_n = b_n.\) So \(y(x,t)= \sum\limits_{n \text{ odd}} \dfrac{8kl^2}{n^3\pi^3} \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right).\)}\) (3 Marks)
\(\text{Write first few terms: \(y(x,t)= \dfrac{8kl^2}{\pi^3}\left[ \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi c t}{l}\right) + \dfrac{1}{27} \sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi x}{l}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi c t}{l}\right) + \cdots \right].\)}\) (1 Mark)
lq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{A string of length  \(l\)  is fixed at both ends. It is pulled into the shape \( y(x,0)= f(x) = kx(l-x)\)}\\ \text{and released from rest. Find the displacement \( y(x,t).\)}\)

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
\(\text{Initial shape: triangular. For \(0\leq x\leq l/2\): \(y(x,0)= \dfrac{2h}{l}x\); for \(l/2\leq x\leq l\): \(y(x,0)= \dfrac{2h}{l}(l-x).\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Wave equation with BCs: \(y(0,t)=0\), \(y(l,t)=0\), \(y_t(x,0)=0.\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{General solution: \(y(x,t)= \sum C_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right).\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(y(x,0)= \sum C_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) = f(x)\) (piecewise linear).}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{Fourier sine coefficients: \(C_n = \dfrac{2}{l} \int_0^l f(x) \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) dx = \dfrac{2}{l}\left[ \int_0^{l/2} \dfrac{2hx}{l} \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) dx + \int_{l/2}^l \dfrac{2h}{l}(l-x) \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) dx \right].\)}\) (3 Marks)
\(\text{Compute integrals: after integration, \(C_n = \dfrac{8h}{n^2\pi^2} \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi}{2}\right).\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Thus \(\sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi}{2}\right) = 0\) for \(n\) even, \(= (-1)^{(n-1)/2}\) for \(n\) odd. So \(C_n = \dfrac{8h}{n^2\pi^2} (-1)^{(n-1)/2}\) for \(n\) odd.}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Hence \(y(x,t)= \dfrac{8h}{\pi^2} \sum\limits_{n \text{ odd}} \dfrac{(-1)^{(n-1)/2}}{n^2} \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right).\)}\) (2 Marks)
